section_header: AUTOMATIC TRANSMISSION — Component Groups (Torque Converter, Electrical Parts)
title: Component Groups (Torque Converter, Electrical Parts)

content.description: Illustration showing hands testing a one-way clutch, with one hand holding the clutch housing and the other rotating the inner component

content.text: The clutch should lock when turned counterclockwise, and should rotate freely and smoothly clockwise. Less than 25 kg-cm (22 in.-lb, 2.5 N·m) of torque should be required to rotate the clutch clockwise. If necessary, clean the converter and retest the clutch. Replace the converter if the clutch still fails the test.

content.description: Illustration showing an ohmmeter connected to a solenoid, testing resistance between terminal and body

content.text: Check the resistance between the terminal and body.

content.description: Illustration showing neutral start switch with terminal layout, displaying terminals labeled R, B, N on left side and L, C, 2 on right side

content.text: Using an ohmmeter, check the continuity of the terminals for each switch position shown in the table below. If continuity between the terminals is not as specified, replace the switch.

content.description: Illustration showing an ohmmeter connected to a speed sensor for testing

content.text: Connect an ohmmeter to the speed sensor and check that the meter deflects when the sensor is repeatedly brought close to the rotor sensor magnet and removed from it.
